summary: Cross-tenant microthrottling causing intermittent throughput collapse in Dedicated pool (us-west)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer QuantizeAI reports repeated short-duration collapses in sustained throughput on their Dedicated GPU pool in us-west. Over the last 36 hours they observed 3–8 minute drops where tail latency spikes and throughput falls to ~20% of provisioned capacity despite apparently healthy GPU memory and normal average utilization.

Impact:
- Customer report: production batch inference jobs degrade intermittently, affecting SLAs for their end users (timeouts and retries).
- Observable: request success rate drops, streaming connections get disconnected during drops, error rate (5xx) increases by ~4–6x during events.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: d-pool-quantize-01 (reserved), region us-west, GPU type A100-80GB (mixed instance types), model pinned to gpt-large-v1.
- Autoscaler: adaptive mode with min_replicas=4, max_replicas=12, scale_window=30s initially.
- Routing: tenant routing with per-tenant queueing and fallback to compatible variants.

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Run a steady stream of small requests (avg request size ~150 tokens) from multiple clients across tenants.
2) Add an intermittent burst generator that sends 400 short requests over 30s every 90s.
3) Observe throughput and tail latency in Grafana panels (Serving -> per-pool QPS/latency).

Logs / observations attached to ticket:
- Grafana snapshot: throughput_spike_and_drop_2026-03-09.png (linked in comments).
- Traces show long scheduling wait times in front of the runtime (scheduling.latency).
- Node metrics: GPU memory stable (~60–70%), gpu_utilization variable; host CPU load shows short spikes coincident with throughput drops.
- Autoscaler logs show frequent scale-down followed by scale-up cycles during events (allocation churn).

Initial hypothesis:
- Short, high-frequency bursts from one or more tenants cause rapid fluctuations in the scheduler's queue length metric. The autoscaler interprets this as sustained change, leading to micro-scale down/up decisions and allocation churn that temporarily starves steady traffic (microthrottling).
- Alternatively, a co-tenant workload is causing driver/kernel-level context thrash or short-lived device resets that are not surfaced as GPU OOMs but increase host-side latency.

Requested customer impact data:
- Time windows when customer saw impact (provided): 2026-03-08 22:12–22:20 UTC, 2026-03-09 03:41–03:48 UTC, 2026-03-09 12:17–12:24 UTC.

Next steps planned:
- SRE to reproduce in staging using a burst generator (assigned to Marco).
- Apply temporary mitigation in prod: increase autoscaler min_replicas to 6 and add a 90s debounce to scale-down to prevent immediate eviction on short spikes.
- Add tenant-level QoS cap to limit burst concurrency for tenants that exceed X rps for > Y seconds.
- Instrument more fine-grained scheduler metrics and add alert on allocation-churn > threshold.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer escalation. Provided initial Grafana links and trace IDs. Asked SRE to triage urgency.
2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Confirmed receipt. Spun up staging repro with burst generator. Requested exact burst pattern from customer and sample request IDs.

2026-03-10 QuantizeAI (support contact - Nina Cho): Provided additional logs and a recording of their load generator showing bursts at ~90s intervals. Confirmed model pinned to gpt-large-v1 and no recent config changes on their side.
2026-03-11 Marco Ruiz: Staging repro completed. Observed identical allocation churn and temporary throughput collapse. Created profiling dump and linked to PR candidate for autoscaler debounce.

2026-03-12 SRE Team Channel (#support): Noted correlation between allocation churn and host CPU scheduling spikes. Hypothesis leaning to scheduler/autoscaler feedback loop rather than hardware failure. Requested scheduler maintainers review allocation window logic.
2026-03-13 Marco Ruiz: Applied prod mitigation: increased min_replicas to 6 and set scale-down debounce to 90s. Customer confirmed reduced frequency and severity of disruptions; monitoring for 48h.
2026-03-13 Aisha Patel: Communicated mitigation and next-steps to customer. Scheduled follow-up for postmortem and longer-term fixes.
investigation_notes: Repro in staging: running two tenants (steady stream tenant + burst tenant) reproduced throughput collapse within 2 cycles. Profiling shows scheduler allocation requests spike then cancel frequently.
Autoscaler logs: recorded scale-down decisions occurring ~15s after a short quiet period, followed by immediate scale-up when burst resumes; scale_window=30s too aggressive for bursty workloads.
Scheduler traces: allocation-granularity set to per-pod with <1s reconciliation loop; leads to high API churn during burst patterns.
Node telemetry: no GPU ECC errors or memory OOMs; host CPU and kubelet metrics show short-lived CPU saturation on nodes hosting the burst tenant which increases container scheduling latency.
Affected workload pattern identified: small, high-frequency requests (150 tokens) in bursts of ~400 requests over 30s every ~90s from a single tenant. This pattern amplifies scheduler churn.
Temporary mitigation applied: min_replicas bump and scale-down debounce. Immediate effect: fewer oscillations, median throughput restored; some residual latency spikes remain during bursts.

Longer-term fixes proposed: 1) scheduler change to batch allocation decisions with 60–120s window for dedicated pools; 2) autoscaler algorithm change to weigh recent volatility and ignore transients <Xs; 3) tenant QoS enforcement feature (per-tenant concurrency caps) to prevent single tenant from causing pool-level churn.
Related PRs: serving-runtime fix to expose additional scheduling metrics (PR #812), scheduler debounce and reconcilation changes (PR #410).
resolution: Mitigation applied in prod 2026-03-13: increased autoscaler min_replicas to 6 and enabled a 90s scale-down debounce for the affected pool. Customer reports visible improvement; monitoring period set to 48h. Next actions: implement scheduler batching and autoscaler transient-guard patch (linked PRs), roll out tenant QoS cap as opt-in for dedicated pools, and schedule postmortem with QuantizeAI. Owner for permanent fixes: Marco Ruiz (scheduler) and Priya Desai (autoscaler).
